events.content:
I've implemented the Dashboard component. It type-checks and `next build` succeeds. I then removed the build artifacts, so the only changes are in `app/Dashboard.tsx` and `app/page.tsx`.

**`app/Dashboard.tsx`**
- It uses the same pattern as `getParallelData` in `page.tsx`. A `getDashboardData()` function fetches `/api/analytics`, `/api/notifications` and `/api/settings` at the same time with `Promise.all`. If a request fails it falls back to mock data, which is what happens during the build.
- It shows the analytics numbers, the notifications list with an unread count (unread ones in bold), and the settings.
- It exports a `preload()` function that starts the requests early.

**`app/page.tsx`** (small change)
- `Page` now calls `preloadDashboard()` before it waits for its own data. Without this, `<Dashboard />` only renders after the page's three requests finish, so the dashboard's three requests would wait behind them. With it, all six run at once. Next.js reuses identical `fetch` calls within a render, so `Dashboard` picks up the requests that are already running instead of sending them again. This is the preload approach from the Next 16 docs.

**Things to check:**
- **API URLs:** server-side `fetch` can't use a relative path like `/api/analytics`, so I build full URLs from `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, which defaults to `http://localhost:3000`. Set it for each deployed environment.
- **The endpoints don't exist yet:** the repo has no route handlers for them. I guessed the data shapes (the `Analytics`, `Notification` and `Settings` types and the mock data), so change them to match the real APIs. If these routes end up inside this same Next app, Next.js recommends that server components call the data logic directly instead of fetching their own `/api` routes over HTTP.
- **Error handling:** as in the existing pattern, if any one of the three requests fails, all three sections show mock data. If you want each section to fail on its own, `Promise.allSettled` would handle that.
